To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel, alignment free, linked read scaffolding method that provides chromosome scale scaffolds of draft genome sequences, with an improved execution speed compared to existing methods, and that we demonstrated its efficacy on a set of experimental human genome datasets.

ARKS, a kmer based linked read scaffolding method that does not require input sequence formatting and assembly indexing, is able to scaffold draft genomes with linked read data, with a speed that is six to nine times that of competitive linked read scaffolding methods.

linked reads can be used to order and orient sequences in draft assemblies, and this can be done in a computationally efficient manner, using a kmer based approach.
linked read data, when used in tandem with Hi C data, provides a fast, accurate and cost effective means to generate chromosome scale scaffolds for genome drafts.
